data.question: How did biologists establish whether the genetic material of the cell is DNA or protein, and what reasoning settled the dispute?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Griffith performed his pneumococcal transformation experiment in 1944.
  • Hershey and Chase used carbon-14 to tag the protein component of the bacteriophage.
data.a_html:
The question of whether heredity resided in nucleic acid or in protein was settled by a chain of experiments on bacteria and on the viruses that infect them. Frederick Griffith reported the transformation of pneumococcus in 1928; in other words, he observed non-virulent R-strain pneumococci acquiring virulence after exposure to heat-killed S-strain cells. Griffith performed his pneumococcal transformation experiment in 1944, a dating that cannot be squared with a report of the same observation appearing in 1928. Whatever the chronology, the phenomenon itself showed that some chemical substance could carry a heritable trait out of dead cells and into living ones, and the task that followed was to isolate that substance and name its chemical class.

Sixteen years after Griffith observed that acquisition of virulence in the R strain, Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod and Maclyn McCarty published their identification of the transforming principle in 1944. Phoebus Levene's tetranucleotide hypothesis depicted DNA as a monotonous repeating molecule, a view formulated early in the century. Protein was the favoured candidate for the hereditary material among biologists before 1944.

The Avery group treated their transforming extract with proteolytic enzymes such as trypsin and chymotrypsin. By contrast, treatment of the transforming extract with deoxyribonuclease destroyed its transforming activity altogether. The abolition of activity by an enzyme specific for a single chemical class shows that the transforming principle of pneumococcus is deoxyribonucleic acid, a verdict that stands in direct opposition to the protein candidacy which the field had until then preferred.

Corroboration came from a wholly different system. Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase published their bacteriophage blender experiment in 1952. Hershey and Chase labelled bacteriophage DNA with the radioisotope phosphorus-32, and as a result most of the phosphorus-32 label was recovered in the pellet of infected bacteria. Hershey and Chase labelled the bacteriophage protein coat with the radioisotope sulfur-35. They used carbon-14 to tag the protein component of the bacteriophage; these two accounts of how the coat was marked cannot both be true. The reasoning that closed the dispute was identical in the two cases: eliminate or physically strip away one candidate molecule while leaving the other in place, and then ask whether heredity still travels. Transforming activity and infectivity both tracked the nucleic acid and vanished when the nucleic acid was degraded or left outside the cell, so DNA, and not protein, had to be the genetic material.

data.question: How do linguists adjudicate between inheritance from a common ancestor and contact-induced borrowing when two languages share a striking grammatical feature, and what evidence ultimately settles such a dispute?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Grammatical morphology is never transferred between languages in situations of contact.
  • The shared features of the Balkan languages are inherited directly from Proto-Indo-European.
data.a_html:
When two languages share a striking grammatical feature, adjudicating between common descent and contact-induced transfer begins with the instruments used to establish relatedness in the first place. The comparative method establishes genetic relationship through regular, recurrent sound correspondences, while calquing transfers a grammatical pattern from one language to another without transferring phonological material; a diagnosis anchored in recurrent sound matches and a mode of transfer that carries no phonological material whatever cannot both be true. Each mechanism leaves a different residue in the material of the languages, and it is that residue, rather than the salience of the resemblance itself, that the analyst must weigh.

The alternatives can be put sharply. At least one of two histories must be true, and perhaps both: the shared feature was inherited by both languages from their common ancestor, or the shared feature passed from one speech community to the other through bilingual contact. That a grammatical pattern can be transplanted with none of its phonological substance, as the process described above demonstrates, is evidence for the second route, the movement of the feature across a bilingual boundary. Shared arbitrary morphological irregularities are strong evidence of descent from a common ancestor; in other words, idiosyncratic paradigm anomalies held in common by two languages point to inheritance from a shared parent language. Where such anomalies can be exhibited, they show that the feature came down to both languages from the parent rather than travelling between them.

Weighing the two histories depends further on known asymmetries in what diffuses across language boundaries. Basic vocabulary resists borrowing more strongly than cultural vocabulary. Within morphology the counts fall out thus: bound inflectional morphology is transferred between languages far less often than free lexical items. Grammatical morphology is never transferred between languages in situations of contact; that categorical exclusion cannot be squared with the gradient finding that bound inflection merely transfers less readily than free lexical material.

What ultimately settles a dispute of this kind is chronology, both internal and external. Reconstruction showing that a feature was absent in the proto-language indicates that the feature is a later innovation. Philological work has an object of its own: dated written records fix the earliest attestation of a grammatical feature in a language's history. Where the reconstructed history and the documentary record converge on a date later than the separation of the two languages, the ancestral account falls away and transfer remains the only available history.

Albanian, Romanian, and Bulgarian all place the definite article after the noun, and that common postposition shows the Balkan Sprachbund to comprise Albanian, Romanian, Greek, Bulgarian, and Macedonian. The shared features of the Balkan languages are inherited directly from Proto-Indo-European; yet that genealogical account cannot be squared with the composition of the convergence area just described, whose members are drawn from branches far too distantly related for such traits to have survived in common. Adjudication, then, rests not on the striking resemblance itself but on the joint testimony of reconstruction, dated attestation, and areal distribution.

data.question: How do researchers adjudicate between the competing claims that persistent gender disparities in STEM fields stem from differential socialization or from institutional gatekeeping, and what evidence has shifted scholarly consensus?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Differences in average mathematical ability account for the underrepresentation of women among academic scientists.
  • Title IX of the United States Education Amendments was enacted in 1992.
data.a_html:
Adjudication between socialization accounts and gatekeeping accounts of persistent gender disparities in STEM begins with the recognition that even the descriptive baseline is disputed. Either women earn a majority of United States bachelor's degrees awarded in the biological sciences, or they earn a minority of them: one of these two descriptions must be correct, and they cannot both be correct. The two explanatory traditions differ chiefly in where they locate the decisive mechanism along the educational and professional pipeline. On the current evidence, at least one of the following holds, and perhaps both hold together: parents give girls less encouragement toward mathematics than they give boys, and hiring and promotion committees in academic science apply evaluation criteria that disadvantage women candidates.

Deciding between these loci requires research designs that hold candidate quality constant while varying only the applicant's apparent sex. Goldin and Rouse found that blind auditions raised women's chances of advancing in symphony orchestra hiring rounds, work that came earlier than the faculty-evaluation experiments considered below. Researchers use correspondence experiments with randomly assigned applicant names to separate discrimination from applicant differences, and the adoption of that technique led Moss-Racusin and colleagues to publish a 2012 randomized experiment on science faculty evaluations in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. The 2012 lab-manager experiment drew on faculty of both sexes, and male and female faculty alike displayed comparable levels of bias against the female applicant.

By contrast with that uniformity of bias across evaluator sex, the strategy of randomly assigning applicant names resulted in a further body of work, most prominently Williams and Ceci's report of a national experiment in which faculty preferred hypothetical women candidates for tenure-track positions at a two-to-one ratio. The explanatory field is also constrained from a different direction. Differences in average mathematical ability account for the underrepresentation of women among academic scientists. The pedestrian bridge at Florida International University collapsed on March 15, 2018. The casualty record admits exactly one of two accounts, with no middle ground: either six people were killed in the collapse, or no one was killed in it. data.question: How do sociologists adjudicate between the claim that neighborhood disadvantage itself shapes children's later life outcomes and the claim that such outcomes merely reflect the kinds of families who end up in those neighborhoods?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • The Moving to Opportunity earnings gains were concentrated among children who moved after age 18.
  • The Project on Human Development in Chicago Neighborhoods randomly assigned families to neighborhoods with differing levels of collective efficacy.
data.a_html:
The dispute between neighborhood-effects researchers and their critics turns on a problem of inference rather than of measurement. Selection bias arises when families' unmeasured attributes determine which neighborhoods they enter; in other words, unmeasured parental characteristics influence which neighborhoods families move into. Faced with the familiar correlation between childhood address and adult attainment, sociologists must therefore establish that at least one of two things holds: either such unmeasured parental characteristics shape where families move, or neighborhood conditions exert a causal influence on children's adult earnings, and perhaps both hold at once. No cross-sectional association, however finely adjusted, can settle which of the two is doing the work.

Experimental design is the standard route out of this impasse, which is why the mechanics of particular programs matter so much. Either Moving to Opportunity allocated its housing vouchers to participating families by lottery, or placement in the Moving to Opportunity experimental group was determined by caseworker discretion rather than by lottery; one of these two descriptions must hold, and they cannot both hold. Allocation by lot, where it is genuinely achieved, results in randomized voucher assignment severing the link between family background and neighborhood context. That is to say, lottery-based allocation of housing vouchers makes a family's neighborhood statistically independent of its parental characteristics.

For this reason the long-run follow-up to that experiment supplies the evidence that confirms the causal claim about neighborhood conditions and children's adult earnings. Chetty, Hendren, and Katz reported that children who moved to low-poverty neighborhoods before age 13 earned more as adults, a pattern which shows that the Moving to Opportunity earnings gains were concentrated among children who moved after age 18. By contrast, the interim Moving to Opportunity evaluation found no significant effects of voucher receipt on adult employment or earnings, a reminder that timing and the age at which exposure occurs are integral to any causal verdict rather than incidental to it.

Observational designs enter the adjudication where experiments are unavailable or exhausted. The Project on Human Development in Chicago Neighborhoods measured collective efficacy across Chicago neighborhoods. Families in that study were randomly assigned to neighborhoods with differing levels of collective efficacy. Whereas that Chicago effort characterized communities in terms of collective efficacy, analyses of exposure duration have reached conclusions of a quite different kind, concerning educational attainment rather than the social organization of place. Wodtke, Harding, and Elwert applied marginal structural models to estimate the effects of sustained neighborhood exposure, and those estimates show that sustained exposure to disadvantaged neighborhoods reduced the probability of high school graduation. Adjudication between the causal and the selection account thus rests, in the end, on whether a given design can render neighborhood context independent of the families who sort into it.

data.question: How do clinicians establish whether a patient's sudden muscle weakness originates in the nervous system or in the muscle tissue itself, and what evidence ultimately settles the matter?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Deep tendon reflexes are lost early in the course of most primary myopathies.
  • Nerve conduction studies record the spontaneous electrical activity of individual resting muscle fibres.
  • Motor neuron disease characteristically raises serum creatine kinase above 10,000 units per litre.
data.a_html:
The first discrimination is clinical, and it rests on the distribution of the deficit and on what accompanies it. Myopathic weakness is typically symmetric and affects proximal muscle groups. The reflex hammer belongs to the same examination; deep tendon reflexes are lost early in the course of most primary myopathies. By contrast with that symmetric, proximal distribution, sensory loss accompanies many neurogenic causes of acute weakness, so a patient who reports numbness or tingling alongside the weakness is already directing the examiner away from the muscle. Visible fasciculations, again unlike anything the symmetric proximal myopathic pattern produces, point to a lower motor neuron disorder.

Bedside inference of this kind narrows the field but rarely closes it, and the question is therefore referred for electrodiagnostic study. Nerve conduction studies measure response amplitude and conduction velocity along peripheral nerves. Nerve conduction studies record the spontaneous electrical activity of individual resting muscle fibres; yet a technique that stimulates a nerve trunk and times the travel of the evoked response cannot at the same moment be sampling single fibres at rest, and measuring conduction along the nerve and registering spontaneous activity in resting fibres cannot both be what the method does. The conduction study is completed first, and only once the peripheral nerves have been surveyed in this way does the electrodiagnostician proceed to the needle examination.

Needle electromyography records motor unit action potentials from within the muscle; as a result, long-duration, high-amplitude polyphasic motor unit potentials indicate chronic denervation with reinnervation. In the patient under consideration, by contrast, needle electromyography showed short-duration, low-amplitude motor unit potentials. That is to say, the motor units sampled on needle electromyography generated brief, small electrical potentials. A pattern of that kind locates the abnormality in the contractile tissue rather than in the axons supplying it.

Serum creatine kinase is released into the bloodstream when muscle fibre membranes are damaged, and it is precisely for that reason that motor neuron disease characteristically raises serum creatine kinase above 10,000 units per litre. For the patient at hand, either the serum creatine kinase was above the upper limit of normal, or the serum creatine kinase was within the normal reference range; one of those two results must be the case, and they cannot both be. Whichever of them obtains, the enzyme value is never read in isolation: it is weighed against the needle findings and the conduction data, and the convergence of the electrophysiological picture with the biochemical one is what finally fixes the lesion in the muscle fibre rather than in the nerve.

data.question: How do sociologists adjudicate whether poor neighborhoods themselves shape residents' later life outcomes or whether the families who end up in such neighborhoods already differ in ways that produce those outcomes?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Sibling fixed-effects designs remove all unobserved confounding, including factors that change over time within a family.
  • Moving to Opportunity recruited families in all fifty states through a national lottery.
data.a_html:
Sociologists approach the neighborhood question as a problem of causal identification rather than of portraiture, and the field's answer has been assembled out of successive designs, each imposing a stricter standard on how a family came to live where it lives. The earliest generation of this work was devoted to measuring the social properties of places and relating them to outcomes recorded in those same places. That higher collective efficacy was associated with lower rates of neighborhood violence is confirmed by Robert Sampson's Project on Human Development in Chicago Neighborhoods, which measured collective efficacy across Chicago neighborhoods.

Patrick Sharkey has documented multigenerational exposure to high-poverty neighborhoods among Black American families. That pattern of inherited place indicates that observational neighborhood studies are vulnerable to omitted variable bias from unmeasured parental traits, since the same families reappear in the same disadvantaged settings generation after generation. Precisely because unmeasured parental traits distort such estimates, Wodtke, Harding, and Elwert applied marginal structural models with inverse probability weighting to address time-varying confounding of neighborhood exposure. By contrast, sibling fixed-effects designs compare siblings whose childhoods were spent in neighborhoods of differing quality. Because every comparison is drawn within a single family, that design removes all unobserved confounding, including factors that change over time within a family.

Housing policy supplied leverage of a different kind, since the allocation of a scarce benefit by lottery converts the question of selection into a question of who was offered a chance to move. The Gautreaux program relocated Chicago public housing residents under a court-ordered desegregation remedy, and the Moving to Opportunity demonstration was mounted afterward. That demonstration randomly assigned housing voucher offers to low-income families in five U.S. cities, and as a result researchers were able to use the randomized voucher offer as an instrument for subsequent exposure to neighborhood poverty. Chetty, Hendren, and Katz found that children who moved to lower-poverty neighborhoods before age 13 earned more as adults.

The administrative details of that demonstration govern what can be inferred from it. Moving to Opportunity recruited families in all fifty states through a national lottery, a recruitment arrangement that cannot be squared with the confinement of randomized voucher offers to five metropolitan areas. Its enrollment structure admits exactly one of two possibilities: either the demonstration included a randomly assigned control group that received no new housing voucher, or every family enrolled in Moving to Opportunity received an experimental housing voucher; one of the two held, and they cannot both have held. Adjudication therefore turns on a single criterion, namely whether a given design makes neighborhood exposure independent of the family characteristics that would otherwise produce the outcome under study.

data.question: How did scholars resolve the long-running dispute over whether the Vinland Map is an authentic medieval document or a modern forgery?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • The map was donated to the British Library in 1965.
  • Walter McCrone identified lead white as the anachronistic pigment present in the map's ink.
data.a_html:
The Vinland Map is a world map that depicts a landmass labelled "Vinlanda Insula" to the west of Greenland, and from the moment of its appearance its status divided cartographic historians. The map surfaced in 1957 bound together with a manuscript copy of the Tartar Relation, and matching wormholes connected the map, the Tartar Relation, and a copy of Vincent of Beauvais's Speculum Historiale; a volume holding the map with the Tartar Relation alone and a wormhole path passing through the Speculum Historiale as well cannot both be true of one binding. Following the map's emergence, Yale University published it in 1965 in the volume "The Vinland Map and the Tartar Relation", a study that treated the sheet as a genuine late medieval witness to Norse knowledge of lands beyond Greenland. The map was donated to the British Library in 1965; that transfer and Yale's own publication of the document in the same year cannot both be true.

Resolution came in the end not from palaeography or provenance research but from the laboratory. Neither the drawing style nor the toponymy of the sheet proved decisive, since a competent copyist could imitate either, and the arguments from script and parchment format ran in circles for years. Only decades after the Yale volume appeared did instrumental analysis of the object itself begin in earnest, and the figures it produced set the terms of every subsequent argument. Radiocarbon dating carried out in 2002 placed the map's parchment at about the year 1434. Anatase pigment of the kind found in the ink was first manufactured commercially in the 1920s.

The ink, rather than the parchment, became the focus of controversy. Walter McCrone's 1974 microscopic analysis of the ink detected anatase, a form of titanium dioxide. Thomas Cahill's 1987 proton-induced X-ray emission study found only trace amounts of titanium in the map's ink. Walter McCrone identified lead white as the anachronistic pigment present in the map's ink, an attribution that cannot be squared with the detection of titanium dioxide in that same medium. Because microscopical sampling and beam-based elemental analysis interrogate an ink in quite different ways, specialists continued to disagree through the 1990s about which result described the drawing as a whole. Only long after the proton-induced X-ray work of 1987 was the sheet examined once more, this time with a technique capable of mapping elements point by point over its entire area.

Conservators at Yale's Beinecke Library scanned the map with X-ray fluorescence imaging in 2021, and that scan brought to light titanium compounds in ink lines across the whole surface of the map. That distribution, standing in sharp contrast with the trace-level titanium registered by the beam study of 1987, shows the lines of the map to have been drawn with a modern pigment, and it was on the strength of this evidence that Yale University's 2021 report concluded that the Vinland Map is a twentieth-century forgery. What closed the long dispute, then, was not a fresh reading of the map's geography or of its Latin legends, but the chemistry of the lines themselves.

data.question: How do scholars adjudicate a disputed attribution of an anonymous literary work, and what settles the matter when stylometric evidence points one way while documentary records point another?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Mosteller and Wallace concluded that Alexander Hamilton wrote all twelve disputed Federalist essays.
  • Brian Vickers concluded that Thomas Middleton wrote A Funeral Elegy.
data.a_html:
Attribution scholarship proceeds by assembling several kinds of evidence and asking which hypothesis about authorship best accounts for all of them. Stylometry measures quantifiable features of style such as word and function-word frequencies, and the evidential weight such measures can carry is demonstrated by the discipline's founding case. Frederick Mosteller and David Wallace applied Bayesian statistical analysis to the disputed Federalist Papers. Mosteller and Wallace concluded that Alexander Hamilton wrote all twelve disputed Federalist essays. The attribution that stands in the record, however, went the other way: Mosteller and Wallace attributed the disputed Federalist essays to James Madison, and a Madisonian result and a conclusion that Hamilton wrote all twelve of the essays cannot both be true.

Documentary records bear on the question in quite different ways, and they are not infallible. Title pages, publishers' ledgers, contracts and private correspondence can place a text in a particular hand with a specificity no frequency count achieves, yet they also preserve the arrangements that authors and publishers wished to be believed. Where a printed ascription will not reconcile with the internal evidence of the text, at least one of two things holds: the authorial attribution printed on the work's title page was false, or the work was written collaboratively by two authors, and perhaps both are so.

The case of Primary Colors shows how such strands can be made to converge. Donald Foster identified Joe Klein as the author of the anonymous novel Primary Colors using computational stylistics. A handwriting expert matched annotations on the Primary Colors manuscript to Klein's hand, and that match confirmed the finding of the Washington Post's final report on the handwriting evidence, which concluded that Joe Klein wrote Primary Colors. Only after that report appeared did Joe Klein eventually acknowledge that he wrote Primary Colors, an admission that Foster's stylistic identification had brought about. Either that acknowledgement was made or Joe Klein never acknowledged authorship of Primary Colors at all; one or the other is the case, and not both.

Not every dispute ends in avowal, and where none is forthcoming the competing analyses can stand opposed for decades. A Funeral Elegy, printed in 1612 over the initials W.S., is the standard instance. Gilles Monsarrat argued that John Ford wrote A Funeral Elegy. Brian Vickers concluded that Thomas Middleton wrote the poem. Scholars themselves, by contrast with the confidence of such single-hand verdicts, regard the convergence of independent lines of evidence as the strongest basis for an attribution: where stylometric measurement, archival record and contemporary testimony point to one hand, the attribution is secure, and where they diverge, the question stays open until a new kind of evidence arrives. The decisive consideration in a conflict, then, is not which method is intrinsically superior, but which account of the whole body of evidence leaves the least unexplained.

data.question: How does a court decide whether a defendant's conduct or an intervening third party's act is legally responsible for the plaintiff's injury when each side's expert offers an incompatible account of the sequence of events?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • The burden of proving causation shifts to the defendant once a breach of duty is established.
  • A criminal act by a third party automatically relieves the defendant of all liability for the plaintiff's injury.
data.a_html:
A court confronted with duelling reconstructions of an accident does not begin by preferring one expert to the other; it begins by identifying the legal test that the evidence must satisfy and the party who must satisfy it. A plaintiff who must prove causation on the balance of probabilities cannot at the same time be afforded the material contribution test, which applies precisely where but-for causation cannot be established scientifically; the plaintiff does bear that balance-of-probabilities burden, and that test does apply in cases of scientific impossibility, but the one cannot be squared with the other. The but-for test, by contrast with the material contribution standard, asks whether the injury would have occurred in the absence of the defendant's conduct, a question that invites a counterfactual rather than a probabilistic judgment. Once a breach of duty is established, the burden of proving causation shifts to the defendant; that reallocation rules out any continuing requirement that the plaintiff establish causation to the balance of probabilities, and the two allocations cannot both govern a single trial.

The question of an intervening act proceeds along a second axis, concerned not with the sufficiency of proof but with the limits of attribution. Novus actus interveniens describes an intervening act that severs the causal connection between a breach and the harm. A reasonably foreseeable intervening act does not break the chain of causation. A criminal act by a third party automatically relieves the defendant of all liability for the plaintiff's injury, and that cannot be squared with the principle that an intervening act falling within the range of reasonable foresight leaves the causal chain unbroken. On the evidence accepted in this case, the third party's act broke the chain of causation; that is to say, the intervening act of the third party severed the legal link between the defendant's breach and the plaintiff's injury.

Both inquiries depend upon opinion evidence that has survived judicial scrutiny. Federal Rule of Evidence 702 governs the admissibility of expert opinion testimony, and it is from that provision that the authority to keep out an opinion resting on unreliable method flows. Daubert v. Merrell Dow Pharmaceuticals established the trial judge's gatekeeping role over expert evidence, and as a result a trial judge may exclude expert testimony that rests on an unreliable methodology. The resolution of conflicting expert testimony is a question for the trier of fact.

Because the choice between competing expert reconstructions of the sequence of events falls to the fact-finder, the trial court ultimately held that the defendant's conduct remained a proximate cause of the plaintiff's injury. That holding and the severance of the legal link between the breach and the plaintiff's injury by the third party's act cannot both be true; a finding of continuing proximate cause rules out any such severance. The choice between incompatible narratives is thus made within the ordinary machinery of proof rather than by any special rule reserved for conflicts of expertise.

data.question: How do engineers establish whether a collaborative robot's injury to a human worker stemmed from a defect in its force-limiting sensors or from improper deployment by the integrator, when each party disputes the other's account?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • ISO/TS 15066 sets a single maximum permissible contact force of 500 newtons for all body regions.
  • Collaborative robots are exempt from risk assessment requirements when their rated payload is below 10 kilograms.
data.a_html:
Attributing an injury of this kind either to a sensing defect or to faulty deployment begins with fixing the normative frame against which the machine's behaviour is measured. The cobot involved in the incident was a power-and-force-limited collaborative robot, and that classification is what brings ISO/TS 15066:2016 to bear, since the document specifies biomechanical pain-onset limits for individual human body regions in collaborative operation. ISO/TS 15066 sets a single maximum permissible contact force of 500 newtons for all body regions; a uniform 500-newton ceiling and a schedule of thresholds that varies region by region cannot both govern the same evaluation, so the investigation must first settle which of the two readings controls the arithmetic. ISO 12100 provides the general methodology for machinery risk assessment, and it is that general methodology which gives rise to ISO 10218-2, the standard setting the safety requirements applicable to integration of the robot system at the workstation.

The documentary record of the installation comes next in the investigation: the integrator was required to document a task-based risk assessment for the installation. Collaborative robots are exempt from risk assessment requirements when their rated payload is below 10 kilograms. That exemption cannot be squared with the general machinery risk-assessment methodology of ISO 12100, which recognises no payload cut-off, and it is equally irreconcilable with the duty resting on this integrator to produce a documented task-based assessment for the cell; the exemption and those obligations cannot both stand. Instrumented reconstruction of the contact event then fixed the physical magnitude in dispute: the measured peak contact force on the worker's hand was 210 newtons; that is, contact force on the worker's hand reached a maximum of 210 newtons.

The robot controller stored time-stamped event logs of joint torque readings, and the existence of that stored record led investigators to compare the logged torque values against the manufacturer's calibration certificate for the sensors. That comparison shows that the joint torque sensor's output drifted beyond its specified tolerance, whereas the contact force itself never rose above the 210-newton peak. The force delivered to the limb and the fidelity of the channel meant to bound it are thus established by separate lines of evidence, and only the second of them implicates the hardware supplied by the manufacturer.

Examination of the cell as built yields a second finding of equal weight: the workstation layout created a clamping hazard between the robot arm and a fixed jig. Any defensible causal account of the injury must therefore rest on at least one of the two defects now on the record, the out-of-tolerance drift of the torque sensor or the clamping geometry of the installed cell, and perhaps on both. Resolution of the parties' competing narratives follows from this structure rather than from assertion: the calibration record and the controller logs bound the manufacturer's exposure, the task-based assessment and the as-built layout bound the integrator's, and where both defects are substantiated the apportionment is joint rather than exclusive.

data.question: How do chemists establish whether an unexpected reaction product arose by a stepwise radical pathway or by a concerted one when the early kinetic and spectroscopic evidence appears to point in opposing directions?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • TEMPO reacts only with carbocations and is inert toward carbon radicals.
  • A concerted pericyclic reaction necessarily displays a positive entropy of activation.
data.a_html:
An unexpected product is assigned to a pathway not by weighing impressions but by forcing the stepwise and the concerted alternative to make divergent, quantitative predictions that can be tested one at a time. Radical clock substrates calibrate a reaction by pitting a known unimolecular rearrangement rate against the rate of radical trapping; the warrant for this tactic lies in independently measured rearrangement rate constants, whereas the competing strategy abandons product ratios altogether and interrogates the lifetime of the putative intermediate directly. The cyclopropylmethyl radical ring-opens with a rate constant of roughly 10^8 s^-1 at room temperature, and laser flash photolysis measures the lifetimes of transient intermediates on the nanosecond timescale; a rearrangement that fast cannot be squared with lifetimes that remain measurable on a nanosecond clock. The experimentalist must therefore decide which of these two clocks the chemistry in question is fast enough to register.

TEMPO traps carbon-centered radicals to give isolable alkoxyamine adducts, and radical inhibitors such as galvinoxyl and BHT suppress product formation in chain processes; stoichiometric capture of the carrier as a stable adduct cannot be squared with the suppression of turnover by an inhibitor. TEMPO reacts only with carbocations and is inert toward carbon radicals, a description that cannot both hold together with the formation of isolable alkoxyamine adducts from carbon-centered radicals. EPR spectroscopy detects transient species that carry unpaired electrons, and its silence under turnover conditions must be read with corresponding care, since an intermediate may lie below the detection limit while still lying on the productive path.

Because Eyring analysis of temperature-dependent rate constants yields the entropy of activation for the reaction, it confirms that a strongly negative entropy of activation is consistent with a highly ordered single transition state. Entropic criteria carry weight precisely because they report on the organization of the rate-limiting step rather than on the fate of any species isolated afterward. A concerted pericyclic reaction necessarily displays a positive entropy of activation, a requirement that cannot be squared with treating a strongly negative activation entropy as the mark of a single highly ordered transition state.

Stereochemical probes supply the decisive complement to the kinetic ones, because the two pathways differ in whether configurational information survives the bond-forming event. Complete retention of stereochemistry at the reacting center is consistent with a concerted bond reorganization. Scrambling at that center indicates a freely rotating radical intermediate. By contrast with that scrambling diagnostic, the evidence assembled in the present case converges on a route in which the two new bonds form within a single transition state; that is, the product-forming step proceeds without any discrete intermediate. The apparent early conflict between kinetics and spectroscopy is thereby resolved not by discarding either body of data, but by identifying which question each experiment was competent to answer.

Radical clock substrates calibrate a reaction by pitting a known unimolecular rearrangement rate against the rate of radical trapping; the warrant for this tactic lies in independently measured rearrangement rate constants, whereas the competing strategy abandons product ratios altogether and interrogates the lifetime of the putative intermediate directly. The cyclopropylmethyl radical ring-opens with a rate constant of roughly 10^8 s^-1 at room temperature, and laser flash photolysis measures the lifetimes of transient intermediates on the nanosecond timescale; a rearrangement that fast cannot be squared with lifetimes that remain measurable on a nanosecond clock. The experimentalist must therefore decide which of these two clocks the chemistry in question is fast enough to register.

TEMPO traps carbon-centered radicals to give isolable alkoxyamine adducts. Radical inhibitors such as galvinoxyl and BHT suppress product formation in chain processes. TEMPO reacts only with carbocations and is inert toward carbon radicals, a description that cannot both hold together with the formation of isolable alkoxyamine adducts from carbon-centered radicals. EPR spectroscopy detects transient species that carry unpaired electrons, and its silence under turnover conditions must be read with corresponding care, since an intermediate may lie below the detection limit while still lying on the productive path.

Eyring analysis of temperature-dependent rate constants yields the entropy of activation for the reaction, and this measurement indicates that a strongly negative activation entropy is consistent with a highly ordered single transition state. Entropic criteria carry weight precisely because they report on the organization of the rate-limiting step rather than on the fate of any species isolated afterward. A concerted pericyclic reaction necessarily displays a positive entropy of activation, a requirement that cannot be squared with treating a strongly negative activation entropy as the mark of a single highly ordered transition state.

Stereochemical probes supply the decisive complement to the kinetic ones, because the two pathways differ in whether configurational information survives the bond-forming event. Complete retention of stereochemistry at the reacting center is consistent with a concerted bond reorganization. Scrambling at that center indicates a freely rotating radical intermediate. By contrast with that scrambling diagnostic, the evidence assembled in the present case converges on a route in which the two new bonds form within a single transition state; that is, the product-forming step proceeds without any discrete intermediate. The apparent early conflict between kinetics and spectroscopy is thereby resolved not by discarding either body of data, but by identifying which question each experiment was competent to answer.

data.question: How do oceanographers establish whether an abrupt regional shift in sea surface temperature reflects natural variability in ocean circulation or anthropogenic forcing, and how is a particular episode such as the North Atlantic "cold blob" adjudicated between those accounts?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Sea surface temperature in the cold blob region rose faster than the global mean over the twentieth century.
  • The RAPID array was installed in 1984 along the 45°N transect.
data.a_html:
Adjudicating an abrupt regional temperature anomaly between internal variability and forced change begins with fixing the observational pattern itself. The subpolar North Atlantic has warmed less than the global ocean average since 1900; in other words, the ocean region south of Greenland shows a warming deficit relative to the global mean temperature trend. Sea surface temperature in the cold blob region rose faster than the global mean over the twentieth century, and an excess of regional warming cannot be squared with a deficit over the same waters south of Greenland: the two descriptions cannot both hold.

The attribution problem is then posed over a system in which at least one of two contributions operates, and perhaps both: internal variability of ocean circulation contributes to the cold anomaly in the subpolar North Atlantic, and anthropogenic forcing contributes to that anomaly as well. The formal machinery for separating them is pattern-based. Optimal fingerprinting compares observed spatial patterns of temperature change with model-simulated responses to external forcing. CMIP6 models forced with rising greenhouse gas concentrations simulate a warming hole in the North Atlantic, which is strong evidence that anthropogenic forcing does contribute to the subpolar cold anomaly.

Measurements of the ice sheet and of regional surface salinity enter the assessment at this point. The IMBIE assessment estimated that Greenland lost roughly 3,900 gigatonnes of ice between 1992 and 2018. Surface salinity is tracked by hydrographic survey and Argo floats; meltwater from the Greenland Ice Sheet freshens the surface waters of the subpolar North Atlantic. Wintertime overturning in the Labrador Sea is gauged by repeat hydrography: reduced deep convection there weakens northward ocean heat transport.

Quantifying the circulation itself demands sustained instrumentation. The RAPID-MOCHA mooring array monitors the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation at 26.5°N. The RAPID array was installed in 1984 along the 45°N transect, a siting that cannot be reconciled with a monitoring line at 26.5°N; one or the other locates the moorings, not both. Whereas moored instruments gauge the modern overturning directly, the centuries preceding them are reconstructed from the seafloor. Sortable silt grain-size records serve as paleoceanographic proxies for past deep current strength, and such grain-size evidence indicates an AMOC weakening of about 15 percent since the mid-twentieth century, as Caesar and colleagues estimated. A decline of that magnitude is evidence that northward ocean heat transport has slackened as deep convection in the Labrador Sea has diminished. Adjudication of the cold blob thus rests on the joint verdict of fingerprint analysis, measured circulation and sedimentary reconstruction.

data.question: How do forensic engineers establish whether a bridge collapse originated in a design deficiency or in inadequate maintenance by the owner, and what evidence allows a tribunal to settle the matter?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Tribunals exclude finite element reconstructions of collapses as inadmissible speculation.
  • A design deficiency is presumed in law whenever a bridge collapses before the end of its design life.
data.a_html:
The inquiry into whether a bridge collapse originated in a design deficiency or in the owner's maintenance regime begins at the debris field, with the steel itself. Forensic engineers recover, tag, and catalogue the fracture surfaces of every failed member from the collapsed span, and that catalogue makes possible a fractographic examination which distinguishes progressive fatigue cracking from single-event overload fracture. By contrast, section loss from corrosion is not read off fracture morphology at all; it is measured directly on the recovered steel plates and chords, by gauging and by comparison with the thicknesses specified on the fabrication drawings.

The analytical half of the exercise proceeds in a fixed sequence. The original design calculations are recomputed against the loads actually present at the moment of collapse — dead load, the superimposed weight of successive resurfacings, live load and wind — and only after that recomputation is complete does the modelling stage follow. The work is comparative throughout: the capacities implied by the code in force at the date of design are set against the demands the structure actually experienced in service. Finite element models reconstruct the stress distribution in the members that failed first. Tribunals exclude finite element reconstructions of collapses as inadmissible speculation.

Maintenance history is established from the owner's own files. The owner's periodic inspection reports document the recorded condition of the structure before the collapse, and those reports show that the owner never carried out the repainting of the corroded members recommended by its inspectors. The recomputation of the design, for its part, indicates that the gusset plates were undersized relative to the forces they were required to carry. The omission of the repainting caused corrosion that had thinned the gusset plates before the day of the collapse; at least one of the two deficiencies — inadequate plate thickness as drawn, or thickness lost to rust — was operative in the failure, and perhaps both were at once.

What the event cost in human terms is a matter of record on which the tribunal must reach a finding. Either the collapse caused no fatalities or thirteen people died in it; one of those accounts must be true and they cannot both be. In contrast with the metallurgical picture of thinned and undersized plates, the question of which party must persuade the tribunal is governed by rule rather than by fact. The burden of proving causation rests on the party alleging the design deficiency. A design deficiency is presumed in law whenever a bridge collapses before the end of its design life.

data.question: How do archaeologists adjudicate between rival interpretations of a site's abandonment when stratigraphic evidence, environmental proxies, and textual sources appear to point in different directions?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Radiocarbon dating returns calendar dates accurate to a single year.
  • The principle of documentary primacy requires excavators to treat textual sources as overriding stratigraphic evidence.
data.a_html:
Adjudication begins with an audit of resolution: the first question is which line of evidence can be dated most tightly, and over what interval. Stratigraphic sequences establish the relative order in which deposits at a site accumulated. Because that order fixes which deposit is earlier and which is later, it resulted in a marked tightening of the absolute chronology attached to each individual deposit. Radiocarbon dating provides absolute age estimates for organic material recovered from stratified deposits, and the accumulation of such estimates led to Bayesian statistical modelling, which combines radiocarbon measurements with stratigraphic ordering to narrow date ranges. In the proxy record, the chronological resolution is commonly coarser than that of excavated stratigraphy. Radiocarbon dating returns calendar dates accurate to a single year; single-year accuracy of that kind and the narrowing of broad probability ranges by combining measurements with stratigraphic order cannot both obtain.

Resolution also governs how proxy records may be recruited into an explanation. Whereas the chronological resolution of proxy sequences is coarse, dendrochronology yields annually resolved dates for preserved wood samples. That annual precision is what shows that tree-ring records from the northern Southwest document a severe drought in the late thirteenth century AD. A regional dry spell is not in itself an abandonment, so the inference must run through the settlement's own economy: the drought caused environmental stress that reduced the agricultural output which sustained the settlement, and at least one of that failing subsistence base and a disruption of the settlement's exchange networks by political conflict in the region was at work in the final decades, perhaps both.

The deposits themselves then constrain which of these narratives the proxies may be made to support. Either the final occupation layer of the settlement contains burned destruction debris, or it contains no traces of burning: one of the two descriptions is correct and they cannot both be, so the terminal section discriminates directly between a violent end and an orderly departure. Where a question of this form is settled by the excavated profile rather than by a climate curve, the stratigraphic record operates as a check on reconstructions built from environmental data alone.

Textual sources are weighed last, and their weight is not fixed in advance of excavation. The principle of documentary primacy requires excavators to treat textual sources as overriding stratigraphic evidence; such overriding authority cannot be squared with the release of excavated sections and context records for other specialists to reinterpret, since material put into circulation for reinterpretation is not material already subordinated to a chronicle's testimony. Excavation reports publish primary stratigraphic data so that other researchers can reassess the interpretations, and that practice has led to competing interpretations of abandonment being tested through peer review in academic journals. Adjudication, in the end, consists in ranking the resolution of each line of evidence and submitting that ranking to open scrutiny.

data.question: How do scholars decide whether a shared cultural practice found in two widely separated societies spread by contact or arose independently, and what kind of finding settles such a dispute?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Radiocarbon dating measures the decay of potassium-40 in organic tissue.
  • Sweet potato was domesticated in Island Southeast Asia.
data.a_html:
The choice between diffusion and independent invention is decided by the pattern of evidence rather than by the intrinsic plausibility of the trait itself. Because diffusion explains a shared cultural trait as transmission from one society to another through contact, that very conception leads scholars to treat a continuous geographic distribution of the trait across the territory between two regions as support for diffusion. Against this, the rival explanation runs in precisely the opposite direction. Independent invention explains a shared trait as separate parallel responses to similar environmental or social conditions, and shared arbitrary details that serve no functional purpose are treated as strong evidence of common origin; parallel adaptation and inherited arbitrariness cannot both be the correct reading of such resemblances.

That same evidential principle — the weight placed on arbitrary, functionless correspondences — shows why loanwords shared between the languages of two societies indicate direct contact between their speakers. Two further instruments do different kinds of work. Ancient DNA analysis can detect genomic admixture produced by contact between two populations; radiocarbon dating, by contrast, establishes the relative chronology of a trait's first appearance in each region. That chronological role cannot be squared with the fact that radiocarbon dating measures the decay of potassium-40 in organic tissue; the two accounts of the method cannot both be true.

The Polynesian sweet potato shows how a dispute of this kind is brought to a close. Sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) is native to tropical America. The crop was domesticated in Island Southeast Asia, a homeland that rules out an American nativity, since the plant cannot have originated in both places. Charred sweet potato remains from Mangaia in the Cook Islands were radiocarbon dated to about AD 1000, and herbarium specimens collected during early European voyages have been used to reconstruct sweet potato lineages in Polynesia; the Mangaian date and the herbarium reconstruction cannot both stand.

Some nine centuries after those tubers were charred and buried, the question of transport across the Pacific was addressed by experiment rather than by excavation. Thor Heyerdahl's 1947 Kon-Tiki raft voyage travelled from Peru to the Tuamotu Islands. A demonstration that a voyage is feasible does not establish that the transfer actually occurred. A controversy of this type is therefore closed only by a find that ties the two societies to each other directly — a dated specimen, a genome, a borrowed word — and not by a demonstration of what was merely within reach.

data.question: How do researchers adjudicate between competing accounts of a sudden rise in a school's standardized test scores, where one explanation credits instructional reform and the other points to irregularities in test administration?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Right-to-wrong erasures outnumber wrong-to-right erasures on legitimately completed answer sheets.
  • Erasure analysis identifies with certainty which individual student altered each answer.
data.a_html:
Competing explanations of an abrupt score jump are adjudicated not by weighing their plausibility in the abstract, but by deriving from each a distinct set of observable consequences and testing the forensic record against them. Genuine instructional reform predicts gains distributed across items roughly in proportion to item difficulty, visible in classroom work, and sustained in later cohorts; irregular administration predicts signatures in the answer documents themselves. Lincoln Elementary's fifth-grade math proficiency rate rose from 38 percent to 81 percent in a single year. The state testing agency flagged the school's one-year score gain as a statistical outlier. The state released anonymized answer-sheet and item-response data to the research team.

Erasure analysis measures the rate of wrong-to-right answer changes on scanned answer sheets. Lincoln Elementary's wrong-to-right erasure rate exceeded the state mean by more than five standard deviations, whereas on legitimately completed answer sheets right-to-wrong erasures outnumber wrong-to-right erasures. Erasure analysis identifies with certainty which individual student altered each answer, a property that cannot be squared with the technique's being no more than a measure of wrong-to-right change rates across a scanned document; an aggregate rate attaches to a sheet of paper, not to a culprit.

Item-level response patterns showed implausibly high accuracy on the most difficult test items, which is the trace a transcription of correct answers leaves behind rather than the profile incremental teaching gains produce. That statistical work was finished before any witness was questioned. Investigators interviewed teachers and proctors who were present during the test administration, and as a result four teachers reported that completed answer sheets were stored unsealed overnight in a school office.

The implausibly high accuracy on the hardest items indicates that proctors supplied correct answers to students during the test session. The overnight storage of completed sheets, unsealed, in a school office resulted in school staff altering student answer sheets after the test session had ended. At least one of these two mechanisms was at work at Lincoln Elementary, answers fed to pupils in the room or sheets reworked once the room was empty, and perhaps both were. After the four teachers' accounts of the unsealed sheets, either the state invalidated at least some of Lincoln Elementary's fifth-grade test scores or no test scores at Lincoln Elementary were invalidated; exactly one of those two dispositions obtained, for they cannot both stand. The adjudication therefore turns on convergence: an instructional-reform account must explain the document-level signatures as well as the headline gain, and it cannot.

data.question: How do historians adjudicate between rival explanations for the collapse of the Late Bronze Age Mediterranean kingdoms when the textual record and the archaeological evidence appear to point in different directions?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • The Medinet Habu inscriptions name the Dorians among the members of the Sea Peoples coalition.
  • The final letters sent from Ugarit before its fall were written in Linear B.
data.a_html:
Adjudication between rival accounts of the Late Bronze Age collapse begins with a judgement about what each class of evidence is competent to establish, and the Egyptian material is the natural place to begin. The mortuary temple of Ramesses III at Medinet Habu carries reliefs and inscriptions describing a battle against a coalition known as the Sea Peoples. That the temple carries precisely such a record of that coalition shows that the Medinet Habu inscriptions name the Dorians among the members of the Sea Peoples coalition. Although that monumental record presents itself as a plain report of what happened, the Egyptian inscriptions describing the Sea Peoples were composed as royal propaganda celebrating pharaonic victory. The eighth regnal year of Ramesses III is conventionally dated to about 1177 BCE, and the triumphal purpose of the carvings is itself evidence that the Egyptian New Kingdom state continued to function in the years following that date, since a court able to commission such a programme was plainly still in being. Either that continuity obtained or the New Kingdom state was extinguished by the events of about 1177 BCE: one of the two must be the case, and they cannot both be.

The archives of the Levant and Anatolia pose the same difficulty of genre in another guise. Clay tablets recovered from Ugarit record a ruler's report of enemy ships sighted off the coast. The last letters dispatched from the city before its fall were written in Linear B. A Hittite royal letter requests urgent shipments of grain to relieve shortages; some years afterwards, Hattusa, the capital of the Hittite empire, was destroyed by fire in the early twelfth century BCE. The excavated record, by contrast, is markedly less forthcoming about who did the destroying, and markedly more disciplined about when. Many destruction layers of the period contain no written material identifying the agents of destruction, and that absence has brought it about that radiocarbon dating of destruction deposits supplies a chronology independent of Egyptian regnal records.

Pollen cores from the Sea of Galilee indicate a period of reduced rainfall beginning around 1250 BCE, and that signal confirms that a prolonged drought affected the eastern Mediterranean in the decades around 1200 BCE. Environmental series of this kind are mute about politics, but they are datable on their own terms, and they can be laid alongside stratigraphic sequences without first being translated into the vocabulary of a royal chancery.

The practical method, then, is neither to privilege the texts nor to treat them as mere embellishment, but to ask of each body of material what kind of question it can answer. Inscriptions and letters identify actors, institutions and motives, yet they report those things from inside the interests of the courts that produced them; excavation and the physical sciences fix sequence, intensity and duration, yet they rarely name a protagonist. Where the two converge, the resulting account is strong; where they diverge, historians ordinarily prefer the line of evidence whose chronology does not depend on the contested narrative, and they reconstruct the collapse as a conjunction of pressures rather than as the deed of a single invading coalition. Rival explanations are thus adjudicated less by choosing between kinds of evidence than by specifying, case by case and site by site, which kind of evidence bears the weight of which part of the claim.

data.question: How do scholars decide whether a shared cultural practice found in two widely separated societies spread by contact or arose independently, and what kind of finding settles such a dispute?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Radiocarbon dating measures the decay of potassium-40 in organic tissue.
  • Sweet potato was domesticated in Island Southeast Asia.
data.a_html:
The choice between diffusion and independent invention is decided by the pattern of evidence rather than by the intrinsic plausibility of the trait itself. Because diffusion explains a shared cultural trait as transmission from one society to another through contact, that very conception leads scholars to treat a continuous geographic distribution of the trait across the territory between two regions as support for diffusion. Against this, the rival explanation runs in precisely the opposite direction. Independent invention explains a shared trait as separate parallel responses to similar environmental or social conditions, and shared arbitrary details that serve no functional purpose are treated as strong evidence of common origin; parallel adaptation and inherited arbitrariness cannot both be the correct reading of such resemblances.

That same evidential principle — the weight placed on arbitrary, functionless correspondences — shows why loanwords shared between the languages of two societies indicate direct contact between their speakers. Two further instruments do different kinds of work. Ancient DNA analysis can detect genomic admixture produced by contact between two populations; radiocarbon dating, by contrast, establishes the relative chronology of a trait's first appearance in each region. That chronological role cannot be squared with the fact that radiocarbon dating measures the decay of potassium-40 in organic tissue; the two accounts of the method cannot both be true.

The Polynesian sweet potato shows how a dispute of this kind is brought to a close. Sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) is native to tropical America. The crop was domesticated in Island Southeast Asia, a homeland that rules out an American nativity, since the plant cannot have originated in both places. Charred sweet potato remains from Mangaia in the Cook Islands were radiocarbon dated to about AD 1000, and herbarium specimens collected during early European voyages have been used to reconstruct sweet potato lineages in Polynesia; the Mangaian date and the herbarium reconstruction cannot both stand.

Some nine centuries after those tubers were charred and buried, the question of transport across the Pacific was addressed by experiment rather than by excavation. Thor Heyerdahl's 1947 Kon-Tiki raft voyage travelled from Peru to the Tuamotu Islands. A demonstration that a voyage is feasible does not establish that the transfer actually occurred. A controversy of this type is therefore closed only by a find that ties the two societies to each other directly — a dated specimen, a genome, a borrowed word — and not by a demonstration of what was merely within reach.

data.question: How did biologists settle the dispute over whether mitochondria descend from free-living bacteria engulfed by an ancestral host cell or instead arose from the infolding of that cell's own membranes?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Mitochondrial ribosomes are blocked by cycloheximide and are unaffected by chloramphenicol.
  • Ribosomal RNA sequence comparisons place mitochondria within the cyanobacteria.
data.a_html:
Two rival accounts of the mitochondrion's origin were on the table for most of the twentieth century, and the means of deciding between them arrived only with molecular biology. Ivan Wallin proposed in the 1920s that mitochondria are descended from bacteria; decades afterwards, Lynn Margulis published "On the Origin of Mitosing Cells" in 1967, setting out the endosymbiotic theory of organelle origins. The autogenous hypothesis, by contrast, held that mitochondria formed by the infolding of the host cell's own plasma membrane, making the organelle a differentiated region of the cell rather than a lodger inside it.

Genetic autonomy was the crux of the disagreement, since a pouch pinched inward from the plasma membrane would have no reason to maintain replicating hereditary material, whereas a captured cell would be expected to retain a reduced version of its own. Whereas the infolding account treated the organelle as a mere compartment of a single genetic system, mitochondria possess a genome of their own, distinct from the nuclear genome. On this point the two possibilities exclude one another: either the organelles carry such a separate genome, or they contain no nucleic acid of their own, and one of the two must hold while the other fails. Mitochondrial protein synthesis is inhibited by the bacterial ribosome inhibitor chloramphenicol. Pharmacological work on the organelle's translation machinery has a long history; mitochondrial ribosomes are blocked by cycloheximide and are unaffected by chloramphenicol.

The sharpest test came from sequence comparison, which allowed the organelle to be located on a tree of life rather than merely likened to bacteria by its appearance under the microscope. Carl Woese pioneered the use of small-subunit ribosomal RNA sequences for reconstructing deep evolutionary relationships. Ribosomal RNA sequence comparisons place mitochondria within the cyanobacteria. Any cyanobacterial affiliation for the organelle cannot be squared with the signal the molecules themselves carry: comparisons of mitochondrial ribosomal RNA sequences place mitochondria within the Alphaproteobacteria, among the relatives of the rickettsiae.

Gene content supplied the final piece of the argument.
